newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says no repo tender on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says no repo tender on Thursday.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it would not hold a tender for short-term securities repurchase on Thursday as current liquidity in the banking sector did not require intervention.

"Based on the latest liquidity developments and the usual figures we decide on, the NBS will not intervene today via repo tender," Peter Andresic, head of the NBS's Open Market Operation Department, told Reuters. "We intervene based on the (key money measure) M2."
The key money measure, M2, rose 19.0 percent year-on-year in November, compared with a 17.9 percent increase in October, the NBS said.
According to official NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector is short of liquidity, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 97.75 percent as of Wednesday.
A new two-week minimum reserve period starts on Thursday.
